headline_findings: The IEEPA tariff stack that dominated 2025 is gone: the Supreme Court held 6-3 on 2026-02-20 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, No. 24-1287, argued 2025-11-05) that IEEPA does not authorize the President to impose tariffs; reciprocal and fentanyl IEEPA duties stopped being collected for all countries from 12:01 a.m. ET 2026-02-24 [verified: Congress.gov CRS LSB11398, Justia 607 U.S. ___ (2026); secondary: Blooming Global, Thomson Reuters].

India's 50% stack (25% IEEPA reciprocal + 25% Russian-oil penalty under EO 14329 of 2025-08-06, effective 2025-08-27) was dismantled before the ruling: an interim US-India trade deal announced 2026-02-02 cut the reciprocal rate to 18%, and an EO signed 2026-02-06 rescinded the 25% penalty effective 2026-02-07 [verified: Federal Register 2025-16419; secondary: Al Jazeera, CNBC, Troutman Pepper].

What surcharge (if any) applies to India-origin goods as of September 2026 was NOT established in this session (WebSearch budget exhausted after 8 queries): the fast statutory stopgap is Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 (max 15%, max 150 days), which my unverified recollection says was invoked in late Feb 2026 and would have lapsed around late July 2026 absent Congress; treat the India-specific surcharge as 'not found / verify' [estimate].

Bluetooth fitness trackers and bands are classified by CBP in HTS 8517.62.00 (statistical suffix 8517.62.0090), MFN duty Free: HQ H279898 (2017-04-05, Fitbit protest; GRI 3(b) essential character = Bluetooth transceiver), NY N291933 (fitness trackers/monitors from China), NY N311614 (electronic smart watch from China); the earlier N068636 (Fitbit Tracker from Singapore) exists but its classification outcome was not visible in the snippet [verified: rulings.cbp.gov].

China-origin 8517.62.00 goods carry Section 301 List 4A +7.5% ad valorem (CBP ruling text states it explicitly); that 7.5% survives the Supreme Court ruling because Section 301 is not IEEPA, and no smartwatch/fitness-tracker exclusion was identified among the 178 exclusions active in January 2026 [verified: CBP NY N311614/N291933 text; secondary: Gateway Lines].

HTS 8517.62.00 was one of the 20 headings on the 2025-04-11 electronics exemption (CSMS #64724565, entries on/after 2025-04-05, secondary code 9903.01.32), so wearables in that heading were never subject to the IEEPA reciprocal duty; whether the India 25% Russian-oil penalty (EO 14329) honoured that exemption is unresolved and matters for any refund claim [verified: CBP CSMS 64724565; secondary: EY].

Section 232 semiconductors: Proclamation 11002 (2026-01-14) imposed 25% only on a narrow set of advanced logic semiconductors from 2026-01-15, with negotiations (report due ~2026-04-14), a 2026-07-01 data-center review, and broader tariffs on derivative products expressly reserved; a separate Section 232 polysilicon action (2026-08-06) sets 15% plus minimum import prices from 2026-12-04 [verified: White House; secondary: C.H. Robinson, White & Case, Lexology].

India export-side numbers (RoDTEP rate for 8517.62, All-Industry-Rate duty drawback, the PMP wearable component-duty ladder, Budget 2025-26 / 2026-27 wearable cuts) were NOT retrieved this session; only structural mechanics are stated from statute knowledge (exports zero-rated under IGST Act s.16 via LUT + ITC refund; SEZ units get duty-free inputs but no s.10AA income-tax holiday for units starting after 2020-03-31) [estimate; verify].

India domestic-sale compliance is known structurally (BIS CRS registration for smart watches under the Electronics and IT Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order; WPC ETA by self-declaration for licence-exempt 2.4 GHz BLE; CPCB EPR registration under the E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022; Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules 2011 declarations; DPDP Act 2023 with Rules notified November 2025 and penalties up to Rs 250 crore) but order dates, fees and floor prices were not verified this session [estimate].

FDA: a screenless band making only fitness/sleep/recovery claims sits under FDA's General Wellness policy (no 510(k), no establishment registration, no FDA import review), but SpO2/blood-pressure/temperature claims framed as diagnosis cross into device territory; WHOOP received an FDA warning letter in July 2025 over its Blood Pressure Insights feature and FDA revised the wellness guidance in January 2026 [estimate: recollection, verify].

Landed cost is tariff-dominated, not freight-dominated: at 150 g shipped a unit consumes 0.15 kg chargeable weight, so even a $10/kg consolidated air rate adds only $1.50/unit, whereas the 7.5% Section 301 line on a China-origin unit adds $1.50 at a $20 customs value and any 10-15% country surcharge adds $2-3; MPF (0.3464% ad valorem, capped per entry) and broker fees are per-entry costs that shrink from ~$0.2/unit at 1k units to ~$0.02/unit at 10k [estimate: arithmetic on explicit assumptions; freight and broker rates not found].

Origin, not final-assembly address, drives the US tariff line: if the PCBA is populated in China and only cased/tested in India, CBP substantial-transformation analysis can still find China origin (Section 301 7.5% + any China surcharge); populating the PCBA in India is the safest route to 'Made in India' for US customs and country-of-origin marking [estimate: CBP origin doctrine, not verified this session].

detailed_notes:
# India policy, tariffs and trade flows for an India-made wearable exported to the US/EU (as of 2026-09-14)

## 0. Method caveat (read first)
This session had a hard cap of 200 WebSearch calls for the whole workflow and only 8 queries executed before the cap was hit; both WebFetch attempts (Thomson Reuters, Blooming Global) returned EGRESS_BLOCKED and curl is blocked. Everything marked **verified** was seen in a government/CBP/Federal Register/White House snippet; **secondary** = trade press/law-firm/analyst snippet; **estimate** = statutory or regulatory facts recalled from prior knowledge (knowledge cutoff June 2026) and explicitly *not* verified in this session, or my own arithmetic. Where I have nothing, the entry says **not found**. The Stage-2 verifier should prioritise the open_questions list.

## 1. US import tariff stack, 2025 -> September 2026

### 1.1 Timeline (verified unless noted)
- 2025-04-05: IEEPA reciprocal tariffs take effect; the same day the electronics exemption (Presidential Memorandum 2025-04-11, CBP CSMS #64724565) removes 20 HTS headings, **including 8517.62.00**, from the reciprocal duty; importers report secondary code 9903.01.32. Wearables classified in 8517.62 therefore never paid the reciprocal tariff.
- 2025-08-06: EO 14329 adds **+25%** on products of India for Russian-oil purchases; effective 2025-08-27 (Federal Register 2025-16419). Stacked with the 25% reciprocal = **50%** (highest of any US partner).
- 2025-11-10: China IEEPA fentanyl tariff cut **20% -> 10%** (CSMS #66749380); China reciprocal stays at 10% with the 34% rate suspended to 2026-11-10 (secondary).
- 2026-02-02: US-India interim trade deal announced; reciprocal rate on India cut to **18%** (secondary: Al Jazeera, CNBC). India reportedly commits to ~$500B of US purchases over 5 years; the joint statement omits the Russian-oil pledge (CNBC).
- 2026-02-06: EO rescinds the 25% Russian-oil penalty, effective entries on/after 2026-02-07 (secondary: Troutman Pepper, ANI).
- 2026-02-20: **Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump (24-1287)**: SCOTUS holds 6-3 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs (verified: CRS LSB11398; Justia 607 U.S. ___). Argued 2025-11-05.
- 2026-02-24 (12:01 a.m. ET): IEEPA reciprocal and fentanyl duties cease for all countries (secondary: Blooming Global). Refund exposure estimated at up to **$175B** (secondary: Thomson Reuters).
- 2026-01-14/15: Section 232 semiconductors, Proclamation 11002: **25%** on a narrow set of advanced logic semiconductors (verified: White House; CBP CSMS #67400472). Negotiation report due within 90 days (~2026-04-14); data-center market update by 2026-07-01; broader tariffs on semiconductors, SME and *derivative products* expressly reserved. Outcome of those reviews: **not found**.
- 2026-08-06: Section 232 polysilicon: **15%** plus minimum import prices, effective 2026-12-04 (secondary: White & Case, Lexology). Upstream only.

### 1.2 India: what applies in September 2026?
The 18% interim-deal rate was an IEEPA rate and died with the ruling. The administration's fast non-IEEPA tools are Section 122 (balance-of-payments; statutory cap **15% for 150 days**, 19 U.S.C. 2132), Section 301 (country investigations, months), and Section 232 (sectoral). My *unverified recollection* is that a global Section 122 tariff was announced within days of the ruling; if invoked ~2026-02-24 its 150-day clock would have run out around 2026-07-23 unless Congress extended it. **I could not verify any of this in-session, so the India-specific surcharge as of 2026-09-14 is recorded as 'not found'.** The verifier should check: (a) the Federal Register for any Section 122 proclamation and its expiry; (b) whether USTR opened a Section 301 investigation of India (or a broad multi-country one) in 2026; (c) whether the US-India interim deal was converted into a non-IEEPA instrument (e.g., a Section 301-based or negotiated rate); (d) whether EO 14329's 25% penalty honoured the 8517.62 electronics exemption between 2025-08-27 and 2026-02-07 (this determines whether any refund is even relevant for a wearables importer).

### 1.3 China: what applies in September 2026?
- MFN 8517.62.00: **Free** (secondary; ITA line).
- **Section 301 List 4A: +7.5%** (9903.88.15). CBP ruling text (NY N311614; same language in N291933) states: products of China classified under 8517.62.00, unless specifically excluded, are subject to an additional 7.5% ad valorem. Section 301 is untouched by the IEEPA ruling. 178 exclusions were active in January 2026 (secondary); no smartwatch/tracker exclusion found.
- IEEPA fentanyl (10%) and reciprocal (10%) were void from 2026-02-24.
- Post-ruling China-specific replacement surcharges: **not found**.
- Net verified differential China vs India at the 8517.62 line as of Sept 2026: **7.5 percentage points** (Section 301) plus any country-specific non-IEEPA measure adopted in 2026 (unknown for both).

### 1.4 Section 232 exposure for a wearable
- Semiconductors: a BLE SoC/MCU (e.g., 40-55 nm class parts used in bands) is not an 'advanced logic semiconductor' in the Proclamation 11002 sense (estimate); the risk is the reserved authority over *derivative products* if the April/July 2026 reviews expanded scope. Verify.
- Steel/aluminium derivatives: Section 232 steel/aluminium (50% since June 2025, recollection) applies to the metal content of listed derivative products; whether any 8517.62 line was added to the derivative lists in the August 2025 expansions is **not found**. A polymer housing with a stainless clip minimises this risk (estimate).

### 1.5 Classification (CBP CROSS)
- **HQ H279898 (2017-04-05)**, protest 4101-2016-100262: various Fitbit wearable fitness trackers -> **8517.62.00**. CBP applied GRI 3(b): the Bluetooth transceiver imparts essential character because it enables display, manipulation and storage of data via the paired smart device (verified).
- **NY N291933**: fitness trackers/monitors and replacement wrist bands from China -> 8517.62.0090 for the trackers (wrist-worn apparatus with accelerometer, displaying and transmitting data sent by a network); the replacement bands appear to be classified separately (search highlight shows 9113) (verified existence; details partly from snippet).
- **NY N311614**: electronic smart watch from China -> 8517.62.00 with the Section 301 7.5% statement (verified).
- **N068636 (2009)**: 'Fitbit Tracker from Singapore' - exists; outcome not visible. This is the ruling most likely to show the older **9029.10 (pedometer)** treatment for a non-transmitting step counter; the 8517.62 result depends on the device having a Bluetooth/radio transceiver. **9031.80** (other measuring instruments) was not seen in any ruling this session. A screenless BLE band with HR/HRV/temperature sensing and BLE sync will follow the Fitbit line into **8517.62.0090** (estimate based on the H279898 reasoning); a ruling request (19 CFR Part 177) is cheap insurance.
- Marking/origin: 19 U.S.C. 1304 requires 'Made in India' marking; origin is determined by substantial transformation. If the PCBA is populated in China and only cased, flashed and tested in India, CBP can find China origin (estimate, consistent with CBP smartphone-origin rulings) - which would import the 7.5% Section 301 line and any China surcharge. Populate the PCBA in India.

### 1.6 Comparison table (US tariff stack on a BLE fitness band, HTS 8517.62.0090, September 2026)
| Origin | HTS | MFN | Section 301 | IEEPA (reciprocal/fentanyl) | Section 232 | Post-ruling replacement | Verified stack today | Notes/source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| India | 8517.62.0090 | 0% | none | void since 2026-02-24 (was 25%+25% Aug 2025 -> 18% Feb 2026) | semis: narrow, likely n/a | not found (Section 122 15%/150d recollection; expiry ~Jul 2026) | **0% + [unknown]** | Fed. Reg. 2025-16419; CRS LSB11398; Al Jazeera |

## 2. India export side
- **GST**: exports are zero-rated supplies (IGST Act s.16). Two routes: export under LUT without paying IGST and claim refund of unutilised input tax credit (CGST Rules r.89), or pay IGST and claim automatic refund via the shipping bill (r.96). Domestic GST on smart watches believed 18% - not verified (estimate).
- **RoDTEP** (DGFT Appendix 4R; remission of embedded taxes as transferable e-scrips): rate for 8517.62 **not found**; whether the scheme is operative for FY2026-27 and for SEZ/AA/EOU units **not found**.
- **Duty drawback** (CBIC All-Industry Rate schedule): rate/cap for 8517 **not found**. Brand-rate drawback (Rule 6/7) is available if actual duty-paid input content is documented.
- **SEZ vs DTA** (estimate): SEZ units import inputs and capital goods duty-free and are outside GST on procurement (zero-rated supplies to SEZ), but the s.10AA income-tax holiday is unavailable to units that commenced after 2020-03-31 and DTA clearances attract full customs duty on the finished good; for a start-up whose volumes are small and whose India sales matter, a DTA unit using Advance Authorisation/EPCG or IGCR duty-exemption for export inputs is usually simpler. Verify current SEZ rules (a 2025 SEZ Rules amendment on DTA sales for semiconductor/electronics units is recalled but not verified).
- **Component import duties (PMP)**: Budget 2022-23 introduced a graded (phased) BCD structure for wearable/hearable inputs (PCBA, charger/adapter, battery, display etc.) escalating year by year to push local assembly. Current FY2025-26/26-27 rates: **not found**. The prompt's 'PCBA 15%' anchor is unverified. Budget 2025-26 is recalled as exempting capital goods for mobile-phone battery manufacturing rather than wearable parts; Budget 2026-27 changes: not found.

## 3. India compliance for domestic sale (all estimate/recollection; dates and fees to verify)
- **BIS CRS**: smart watches are in the CRS product list under the Electronics and IT Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order (2012 order, expanded 2019-2021; consolidated 2021 order); safety standard IS 13252(Part 1) with transition to IEC 62368-1-based IS. Registration requires testing at a BIS-recognised lab, a licence per brand/model family, and the R-number on the label. A screenless band is still a 'smart watch/wearable' for CRS purposes - obtain a scope confirmation. The Li-ion cell needs its own CRS registration (IS 16046) if imported as a cell.
- **WPC ETA**: BLE at 2.4 GHz is a licence-exempt band; ETA by self-declaration on Saral Sanchar; no WPC import licence for licence-exempt equipment. Fee not found.
- **E-waste**: E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022 (effective 2023-04-01): producer registration on the CPCB EPR portal, annual returns, EPR certificates bought from registered recyclers; recalled targets 60% (FY24), 60% (FY25), 70% (FY26), 80% (FY27 onward) of the weight placed on market in the reference year; a 2024 amendment introduced minimum EPR-certificate prices - value not found.
- **Legal Metrology**: Packaged Commodities Rules 2011 declarations (manufacturer/importer name and address, generic name, net quantity, MRP inclusive of all taxes, month/year of manufacture or import, consumer-care contact, country of origin on imports; unit sale price where applicable); importers need LMPC registration; e-commerce listings must carry the same declarations.
- **DPDP Act 2023 + Rules (notified November 2025)**: applies to digital personal data incl. health data (no separate sensitive category); requires notice + consent, purpose limitation, security safeguards, breach notification to the Data Protection Board and affected users, data-principal rights (access, correction, erasure), verifiable parental consent under 18; cross-border transfers allowed except to countries the government blacklists; possible 'Significant Data Fiduciary' designation; penalties up to Rs 250 crore for security-safeguard failures. Phased commencement (12-18 months for most obligations, recollection). FitForge's local-first/no-silent-sync rule already fits the consent-first design; the device firmware-to-app path should keep raw health data on-device.
- **China-sourced components**: no anti-dumping duty specific to wearable PCBAs/sensors was identified (not found). Structural constraints: Press Note 3 (2020) government-approval route for equity from land-border countries; BIS CRS on Li-ion cells; MeitY's trusted-source regime does not apply to consumer wearables (estimate).

## 4. Logistics and landed cost (worked example; inputs are explicit assumptions)
Assumptions: customs value (transaction value, FOB) **$20/unit**; device 60 g, shipped 150 g in retail box; retail box ~12x8x5 cm = 480 cm3 -> volumetric weight 80 g at 6,000 cm3/kg, so actual weight governs; chargeable weight 0.15 kg/unit; 1,000 units = 150 kg, 10,000 units = 1,500 kg. Air freight rate **not found**; sensitivity $3 / $6 / $10 per kg -> $0.45 / $0.90 / $1.50 per unit. Courier (DHL/FedEx 1-10 kg) rates **not found**; only for samples.

US side per unit (India origin, no surcharge): value 20.00 + freight 0.90 + duty 0.00 + MPF 0.07 (0.3464% x $20; the per-entry cap binds at 10k units) + broker ~0.15 at 1k units (assumed $150/entry, not found) = **~$21.12**; at 10k units ~**$20.99** (MPF capped per entry + broker amortised ~$0.08 combined). Add **$2.00/unit per 10 points** of any India surcharge that turns out to apply (i.e., $3.00 at a 15% Section-122-style rate).
China origin: add 7.5% Section 301 = $1.50 -> **~$22.62** (1k) / **~$22.49** (10k), before any post-ruling China surcharge (not found). Not included: cargo insurance (~0.3-0.5% of value, assumption), US-side inland delivery, FCC/UL testing amortisation, and Indian-side RoDTEP/drawback credits (rates not found).
US customs entry: formal entry required above $2,500; de minimis ($800) suspended for all countries from 2025-08-29 under EO 14324 and repealed by statute from 2027-07-01 (recollection) - DTC single-unit shipping from India cannot rely on it. FDA: a general-wellness band needs no FDA prior notice or listing; the broker files a 'not FDA-regulated' disclaim if the HTS line is FDA-flagged (estimate).
EU side: 0% duty, import VAT at destination rate (recoverable for a registered business or collected via IOSS for B2C); CE marking under RED 2014/53/EU including the cybersecurity delegated act applicable since 2025-08-01, RoHS, WEEE and Battery Regulation registrations; GDPR Art. 9 treats health data as special-category (recollection).

## 5. India vs China vs Vietnam vs Mexico (mostly not retrieved)
- Trade-press comparisons (Counterpoint 'Make in India' wearables share, ICEA reports, 'China+1' surveys): **not found** this session.
- Labour (estimate): Vietnam Region I minimum wage VND 4.96M/month from 2024-07-01 (recalled +7.2% to ~VND 5.31M from 2026-01-01); Mexico MXN 278.80/day (2025), ~315.04/day (2026); Shanghai RMB 2,690/month (2023-07). India operator wage of Rs 15-25k/month and China RMB 5-7k are the owner's assumptions - unverified; note both are gross with overtime, not minimum wages.
- Electricity reliability and industrial tariffs: **not found**; EMS clusters (Sriperumbudur, Noida, Hosur) run DG/UPS backup as standard practice (estimate).
- Component lead times / customs clearance days into India: **not found**; CBIC's National Time Release Study series is the root source (air cargo release times are reported in hours).
- Quality perception: no sourced data; Indian smartwatch brands (boAt, Noise, Fire-Boltt) moved assembly onshore in 2023-2024 largely on Chinese ODM designs (recollection).

## 6. What this means for the FitForge band decision
1. Tariff advantage of India over China at the 8517.62 line is currently the verified **7.5-point Section 301 gap**, not the 25-50-point IEEPA gap of 2025; the 2026 replacement regime is the swing factor and is unknown.
2. Origin must be earned by populating the PCBA in India, or the advantage evaporates.
3. Freight is a rounding error at 150 g; per-entry fees push toward consolidated shipments of >=1,000 units.
4. India-side incentives (RoDTEP/drawback/PMP) are unquantified here - a 1-2% swing at most on FOB, so second-order versus tariffs (estimate).
5. Compliance cost drivers in India are BIS CRS testing/registration and DPDP engineering, not customs.
